html:
Stefan Dušan was king of Serbia from 1331 and emperor from 1346 until his death in 1355, ruling the largest state in the Balkans of his day.

He took most of Macedonia, Albania, Epirus and Thessaly from a Byzantine Empire torn by civil war. In 1346 at Skopje he was crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks, after raising the head of the Serbian church to patriarch at Peć. His law code, Dušan's Code, set out the rights of nobles, church and peasants. He was buried in his foundation of the Holy Archangels near Prizren, his favourite residence. He may have hoped to take Constantinople, but he died suddenly at about 47. His empire split among nobles, and the Ottomans advanced.
